notes: §1985:VI.2.3.1 prints a source program as identification-division, then an optional environment-division, data-division, procedure-division and end-program-header, in that order and each once; §1985:VI.3.1 adds "The Identification Division is required in a COBOL source program." The grammar rule programUnit is that sequence (the nested programs between the Procedure Division and the end marker are the Inter-Program module's extension of the format), so a division out of order, repeated or written without its header is a syntax error at every edition. The one 1985 arm is the header: identificationDivision parses the header as optional (the 2023 bracket), and VersionConformancePass.VisitIdentificationDivision refuses a unit that opens on PROGRAM-ID below 2002 (construct identification-header-optional-2002, COBOL0900). endProgramHeader also parses END FUNCTION, which SourceUnitShape.Screen refuses on a program (COBOL2274). The witness compiles and runs a program of an Identification and a Procedure Division. Probed further at --std 85: a unit starting at PROGRAM-ID draws COBOL0900; a unit starting at ENVIRONMENT DIVISION, DATA before ENVIRONMENT, DATA after PROCEDURE, a second ENVIRONMENT, DATA or PROCEDURE DIVISION, WORKING-STORAGE with no DATA DIVISION header, a division after the end program header, and ID DIVISION each draw a syntax error; the Identification Division alone, with an end program header, with empty Environment and Data Divisions, all four divisions with the header, and two programs in sequence separated by an end program header are accepted.

next.reason: 1985: identification-division [environment-division] [data-division] [procedure-division] [end-program-header] (the end marker a level-2 element). §2023:10.6.1 program-definition keeps the order and the optional END PROGRAM but writes "[ IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. ]" and adds [ options-paragraph ]; §2023:11.2.1 restates the bracketed header. A program starting at PROGRAM-ID, refused in 1985 (VI.3.2.1.1 requires the header), is accepted. End-marker presence rules are 1985 VI.2.3.3 GR2 and X.2.3.2 SR1, mapped separately. Compile-time only.
